world.bio: Senior associate at a mid-size audit firm in Kuala Lumpur, mostly SME audits and a few manufacturing clients in Shah Alam. On weekends I keep the books for my mother's small kuih business for free. Doing a part-time MBA on Saturdays, engaged, getting married in five months. Coffee-dependent, spreadsheet-happy, bad at saying no to my family.
skills_assets: Qualified accountant (ACCA), 8 years in audit, comfortable with SST and corporate tax filings in Malaysia
Autotab-style Excel templates I built for mum's kuih orders: costing per tray, weekly cash-up, supplier ledger
Small circle of audit-firm colleagues and a few SME owners who ask me for favour advice
A Honda City, a ten-year-old laptop, and a very annoyed label printer

projects.name: Mum's kuih business books
projects.text: Mum sells kuih lapis, ondeh-ondeh and seri muka through two pasar malam stalls and WhatsApp pre-orders for Hari Raya and Deepavali. I clean up her notebook every Sunday and enter it into a simple sheet. Cost per tray was a mystery until last month; turns out she was underpricing the pandan ones by about 15 sen each. Still need to convince her to stop paying the coconut supplier in cash with no receipts.

projects.name: MBA part-time, Financial Management module
projects.text: Saturday classes 9am to 4pm at a campus in Petaling Jaya. Group assignment due 24 Oct, group of five, two of whom never reply. I ended up writing most of the valuation section. Professor likes case studies on regional airlines.

projects.name: Wedding planning
projects.text: Wedding is in five months, around 300 guests, Hindu ceremony in the morning then reception in the evening. The reception venue we booked in Mont Kiara went into liquidation and the liquidator says our deposit is an unsecured claim. Now looking for a replacement hall on short notice and trying not to cry in front of my fiance.

notes.text: Audit fieldwork at the Shah Alam client again. Inventory count was a mess, forklift drivers sleeping on pallets. Home at 9.30pm. Mum had kept dinner warm, didn't even ask about my day, just asked if I had eaten. That is love.

Appa's sugar was 11.8 this morning fasting. Doctor wants him on insulin soon. He says he will 'think about it' which means no. Amma is hiding the sweets in the rice drum, which he knows. Need to call the clinic and push for the diabetic educator appointment.

Venue emailed. The company is in liquidation. Deposit RM 18,000, gone unless we file a proof of debt. I do this for a living for OTHER people. Lawyer cousin says do not expect much. Ranjit was calm, which made me angrier.

Sunday kuih books. Mum made 62 trays for a Deepavali pre-order from a bank branch. Margin on seri muka is good, ondeh-ondeh is barely break even because of gula Melaka price. Showed her the sheet, she nodded and said 'so just charge more?' Yes mum. Yes.

Saturday class was wasted: spent half of it on phone calling venues. Hall in Brickfields free on the date but RM 14k for lunch only. Other one in Subang wants 50 percent upfront which I will NOT pay again without reading their accounts.
Dress fitting, tailor says she needs another 2cm of take-in. I haven't been eating well. Meh. Auntie from the temple asked if we've sent invitations yet; we haven't even got a hall.
Quarter-end at the firm. Partner wants me to take on two more files in November. I said I'd see. I'm tired in a way that coffee isn't fixing.
Appa walked 20 mins with me at Taman Tun park, short of breath at the end. Told Amma not to worry him. Booked the educator appointment for 9 Oct.

messages.text: Ranjit: Don't spiral. We pay, we move on, we find another hall. Me: It's RM 18k, that's not nothing. Ranjit: I know. Me: I audit these people! I should have asked for their last financials. Ranjit: You can't audit every aunty's cousin's hall. Me: Watch me.
Amma: Priya, ondeh-ondeh order from Mrs Lim, 40 boxes. Me: Okay I'll cost it Sunday. Amma: Don't cost it, just help me pack. Me: Both. Amma: You are too thin.
Sharmila: File the proof of debt anyway, costs nothing. Me: What's the realistic recovery? Sharmila: Pennies on the ringgit. Me: Great, a wedding gift for the liquidator.
Kelvin: Can you start the Penang client on 10 Nov? Me: I have wedding venue chaos, can we push to the 17th? Kelvin: Fine but don't tell the other seniors.
Daniel: who is doing slide 12? Me: I did slide 12 two weeks ago. Daniel: oh. Me: Please read the shared drive.

calendar.event: Sunday: kuih books at Mum's, Subang Jaya
Diabetic educator appointment for Appa, 9am, Klinik Kesihatan
MBA class (Financial Management) and venue viewing 5pm, Brickfields
Hall viewing in Subang, with Ranjit

relations.about: Type 2 diabetes for 12 years, now worsening. Eats secretly, hates needles. Retired schoolteacher.
Runs the kuih business from a home kitchen, proud, refuses to hire help or take advice about receipts.
Fiance, software tester, calm in a crisis, better at saying no than me.

constraints: Cannot spend more than RM 40k total on the reception after the lost deposit
Saturdays are blocked for MBA classes until December
Will not lie to clients or bend numbers, even for family favours
Not willing to commit to new weekend work before the wedding
sensitive: Her father's fasting glucose and reluctance about insulin
The RM 18,000 lost deposit and how guilty she feels as an accountant
Credit card balance of about RM 9,000 from wedding costs so far
She has been crying in the car park after work, twice this month
